section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the findings of the present study, which investigated the associations between satisfaction with adult children's achievements, geriatric depression/loneliness, and the mediating roles of support from children and gratitude. Results confirmed that satisfaction with adult children's achievements predicted lower depression and loneliness, and also predicted increased gratitude and perceived support from children. Gratitude and perceived support, in turn, predicted lower depression and loneliness. Mediation analyses indicated that gratitude fully mediated the link between satisfaction and loneliness, while children's support partially mediated satisfaction and loneliness, and both partially mediated satisfaction and depression. The study acknowledges limitations including its cross-sectional design, reliance on questionnaires, and a sample predominantly composed of women and less educated older adults.
